items.title: Add salt
items.because: Salt is 2,593 ppm, below the 2800-3200 ppm the cell needs. A cell run under its salt band makes less chlorine and wears out faster.
items.why: Salt is 2,593 ppm against the 2,800-3,200 ppm band the cell needs to make chlorine properly. Run the cell below that band and it makes less chlorine while working harder to do it, which shortens its life.
items.how: Dissolve the salt in batches in a five-gallon bucket of pool water before it goes in, rather than dumping the bag straight onto the liner floor. Pour each batch around the deep end with the pump running so it disperses, and brush off any granules that settle undissolved so they don't sit on the vinyl.

dose.label: 61 lb of salt (about 1.52 of a 40 lb bag)

items.title: Bring pH down
items.because: pH is 7.97, above the 7.6-7.8 target. TA wasn't measured, so this dose assumes a mid-band buffer -- treat it as a starting point and retest.
items.why: pH is 7.97, above the 7.6-7.8 target, and high pH cuts how well your chlorine actually sanitizes even when the level reads fine. TA wasn't measured so this dose assumes a mid-band buffer -- treat it as a starting point and retest pH once it's circulated.
items.how: Fill a bucket with pool water first and pour the acid into that water, never the other way around, then carry it to the deep end and pour it in slowly with the pump running. Never pour it into the skimmer -- neat acid there runs straight through the pump, heater and salt cell and eats them. Retest pH in a few hours since the dose is based on an assumed TA, not a measured one.

dose.label: 27 fl oz (3.38 cups) of muriatic acid

items.title: Backwash the filter
items.because: Never logged. The target cadence is every 14 days -- log it once and the clock starts.
items.why: The filter has never been logged as backwashed, and the target cadence is every 14 days. Logging it today just starts that clock so you know when it's actually due next.
items.how: Switch the valve to backwash, run it until the sight glass runs clear, then flip to rinse for about 30 seconds before going back to filter. Log the date once it's done.

items.title: Empty the skimmer basket
items.because: Never logged. The target cadence is every 3 days -- log it once and the clock starts.
items.why: The skimmer basket has never been logged as emptied, and the target cadence is every 3 days. A full basket restricts flow to the pump, so logging this once starts a cadence you can actually track.
items.how: Pull the Aqua Genie basket, dump the debris, and give it a quick rinse before dropping it back in. Log the date so you know when the next one's due.

items.title: Leave the cell alone for now
items.because: ORP is 403 mV, under the at least 600 mV floor -- but pH and Salt are out of band too, and ORP sits downstream of all of it. Fix those first, give the water a full day to circulate, then re-read. Turning the cell up now just means running it harder against the same problem.
items.why: ORP is 403 mV, well under the 600 mV floor, but it sits downstream of both the low salt and the high pH you're already fixing today. Turning the cell up now just runs it harder against water that's still out of band on two fronts.
items.how: Leave the cell's output setting where it is for today. Let the salt and acid you just added circulate for a full day, then retest ORP before deciding whether the cell actually needs a nudge.

items.title: Test borates
items.because: Borates aren't on the ICO panel and haven't been tested. The target is 50 ppm; a strip test once a season is enough to know where you are.
items.why: Borates aren't on the ICO panel, so the only way to know where you stand against the 50 ppm target is a manual test. It's a once-a-season check, not something that needs constant tracking.
items.how: Dip a borate test strip in the water away from the return jets and compare the color against the chart. No dosing today either way -- this is just a reading to log.

safety_rules: NEVER pour undiluted acid into the skimmer. Acid down the skimmer runs neat through the pump, heater and salt cell and eats them. Dilute it and pour it slowly around the deep end with the pump running.

NEVER put shock and acid in the same session without at least 4 hours between them, and say the gap out loud in the instructions. Both move pH hard in opposite directions, and back to back you cannot tell what the water actually did.
ALWAYS predissolve dry chemicals in a 5-gallon bucket of pool water before they go in. Undissolved granules sitting on a vinyl liner bleach and weaken it.
NEVER put chlorine and acid in the same bucket, in either order. That combination produces chlorine gas.
ALWAYS add acid to water, never water to acid -- pouring water into acid can boil and spit it back at you.
The pump must be RUNNING before anything goes in, and keep running afterwards, so a dose disperses instead of sitting in one corner.
headline: Salt's low and pH is high — dose both today, then leave the cell alone
summary: Fresh reading from this morning: salt at 2,593 ppm is short of the band the cell needs, and pH at 7.97 is pushing high. Add the salt, then bring the pH down as a separate step, keep the pump running through both, and give the water a full day to circulate before touching the cell's ORP problem.
